title: Type Escape Hatches at Security Boundaries
platform_conditions: Type-checker behavior only; any/as/!/@ts-ignore leave no runtime trace and apply wherever the compiled JavaScript runs
security_mechanism: any disables checking for every expression derived from it, so one 'const user: any = JSON.parse(data)' makes the entire downstream call graph unchecked while reading as type-safe. The double assertion 'as unknown as T' converts between unrelated types without an error, non-null '!' suppresses the undefined check exactly where null arrives from attacker-shaped payloads, and @ts-ignore deletes the diagnostic rather than fixing the cause. On an authorization path these constructs let a mis-typed role or missing field flow unchecked into grant/deny decisions.

source_sink_clues.source: External payloads entering through any-typed variables, double assertions, non-null assertions, or @ts-ignore-suppressed lines.
source_sink_clues.sink: any / as unknown as T / ! / @ts-ignore on values that feed authentication, authorization, or privilege fields

tracking_guards: Check the boundary value flows through an explicit validation step rather than a type escape; check strict mode is enabled and escape hatches are counted in CI (no-explicit-any, no-non-null-assertion lint rules); check each suppressed diagnostic has a recorded justification.
not_candidate_when: The escape hatch sits on internal glue code whose value was validated at entry, the '!' guards a field that is structurally guaranteed non-null by a preceding validated parse, or the value is a test fixture never deployed.
public_references: CWE-704: Incorrect Type Conversion or Cast — https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/704.html
TypeScript Handbook: Everyday Types (any and unknown) — https://www.typescriptlang.org/docs/handbook/2/everyday-types.html
